frontmatter.title: Grover search
frontmatter.description: A runnable three-qubit search, a parameterized circuit generator, and explicit logical counts.

children.value: Grover search amplifies the probability of a marked item using a reversible predicate and a reflection about a uniform superposition

. It is a useful first implementation because its circuit is small enough to inspect and its ideal success probability has a closed form. The survey gives the broader application and end-to-end complexity context

The three-qubit demo is simulated and checked against the mathematical prediction during the site build. The generator supports other sizes. The exported circuit includes the oracle and diffuser decomposed into gates; the fixed three-qubit circuit compiles to exact Clifford and T operations, while larger circuits can require arbitrary-angle synthesis. children.value: Every plotted point is a returned estimator result, with its physical qubit count, runtime, factory information, model properties, and instruction provenance preserved in the report. The two summary choices can coincide for a small circuit.

The three algorithm qubits do not translate into three logical compute qubits under the estimator’s scheduling model. Its logical ancillas, data code distance, and factories contribute to the physical count. These overheads can dominate a very small circuit; they are included rather than amortized over an unspecified larger workload.
For this instance, the exported rotations are exact Clifford or T operations. The QDK canonical application trace requires

, with no arbitrary-angle rotation synthesis. The estimator abstracts Clifford work and scheduling into its resource model, so the reported runtime is a model estimate rather than an exact schedule of the original Qiskit circuit. The initial pipeline rejects arbitrary-angle traces until their approximation-error budget is specified.

, 100 ns gate time, and 500 ns measurement time. These are editable model inputs, not benchmarks from a specific processor. The estimator explores the rotated surface-code and round-based factory model combinations and returns a Pareto frontier.

Peak physical qubits remain the per-trial peak because trials run serially. Runtime is multiplied by two. Quantum measurement time is included; classical verification and circuit compilation time are currently unmeasured and excluded. The tests verify that the oracle flips exactly the requested basis state, that simulated success matches the closed form for several register sizes and iteration counts, and that decomposition preserves the unitary up to global phase. These are numerical and functional checks.

provides relevant quantum algorithm proofs in Coq/Rocq; a linked proof does not establish correctness of this Python generator or its surface-code compilation. Any later proof badge must record the theorem, assumptions, pinned proof toolchain, successful proof build, and connection to this circuit.

uses an explicit equality phase oracle, whose marked integer is known to the generator. This is a teaching instance for circuit correctness.

The notebook also checks 30 bounded cases for its live controls. Every interactive evaluation verifies the simulated marked-state probability against the same analytic expression. Saved circuit and probability outputs are reused in the chapter; a static page does not execute the Python controls.
The 13 baseline-contract test cases check repetition arithmetic, allocation between ideal sampling failure and modeled physical faults, and rejection of opaque or unmeasured inputs. The
records the actual circuit digest and assumptions.

The seven general-resource-helper cases separately check static lowering, budget semantics, rejected operations, and the audited arbitrary-rotation model. That helper’s mean-fit projections are conditional and do not certify concrete synthesis sequences. Its tests do not expand the proof scope of the frozen Grover instance.

A practical search predicate needs its own reversible implementation, independent semantic checks, loading cost, and classical verification procedure. An integrated theorem would need to identify its mathematical object, assumptions, toolchain, and connection to this Python circuit. External
are relevant references; this project has not reproduced a proof that covers the implementation and its physical compilation.
